boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Vermillion Bayou record (April 17, 1863) in Operations in West Louisiana [April 1863]. The retreat from Franklin on April 14-16 and the pursuit to Opelousas are context. Campaign-wide movements (the Berwick Bay crossing of April 9-11, the pursuit to Opelousas and Alexandria) and multi-day loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 4th Division, XIX Army Corps, Army of the Gulf [US] and District of Western Louisiana [CS]; the live field reads zero. Irwin says Banks's united force outnumbered Taylor's three to one on April 15, that Grover advanced on the Vermilion with his main body reinforced by Gooding's brigade, and that Taylor's army was melting away by desertion; Taylor says nearly all of Fournet's battalion deserted with their arms. No inspected passage gives a count for the action.
claims.rationale: A ratio and unit identifications from a history and an interested report. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. NPS says Confederate artillery forced the Union troops back and that the Confederates retreated after dark having slowed the advance; Irwin says Dwight drove off the enemy; Taylor says the retreat resumed on Friday.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The accounts differ on the course of the artillery fight.

open_questions: Grover's No. 24, Dwight's No. 30 and Van Zandt's No. 33 reports, the Union nominal lists and any Confederate return for the Vermilion remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' later assistant adjutant-general. Its Teche chapters cite Taylor's report and the nominal lists, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 23, 1863 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XV, a shared container) is an interested Confederate account; it is placed in the group of his 1864 Red River reports as one author family. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
